name: A10-0090/2026 – Moritz Körner – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the European Union, of the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime; Strengthening International Cooperation for Combating Certain Crimes Committed by Means of Information and Communications Technology Systems and for the Sharing of Evidence in Electronic Form of Serious Crimes
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees that the European Union should sign up to a United Nations agreement against cybercrime. The agreement aims to help countries work together against crimes committed online and to share electronic evidence of serious crimes across borders. The Parliament's report says this cooperation matters because the internet has no borders, and it says the agreement must protect human rights and basic freedoms when authorities use it. The report also notes that some civil society groups and service providers criticised the agreement over these protections.

- The EU joins a global deal on fighting cybercrime and sharing electronic evidence.
- It affects police and prosecutors in EU countries and their partners abroad.
- Next, the EU formally concludes the agreement and works to apply its safeguards.
